title: `canonicalize_license_expression` turns `LicenseRef-mit OR licenseref-MIT` into `LicenseRef-MIT OR LicenseRef-MIT`
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

```python
from packaging.licenses import canonicalize_license_expression
canonicalize_license_expression("LicenseRef-mit OR licenseref-MIT")
```
Expected: `'LicenseRef-mit OR LicenseRef-mit'`.
Actual: `'LicenseRef-MIT OR LicenseRef-MIT'`.

When the same reference is written with different casing, I'd expect the spelling of its first occurrence to be used throughout. Similar inputs are probably affected too; please fix the underlying problem rather than just this case.
acceptance: the reported example produces the expected output
the underlying problem is fixed, not just the reported input
